name: Towing & roadside

A.flow: A: the customer comes to the business (video or phone count as A)
A.staff: Remy and Nina (at the yard window)

services.name: Yard car pick-up
services.story: The main story: a car pick-up at the yard window. Nothing is taken: a YES books the time. Alex shows a photo ID and the registration, and pays the $35 storage at the window.

B.flow: B: the business goes to the customer
B.staff: Kyle and Marcus (tow drivers; one is on call each shift)

services.name: Tow
services.story: The main story: a $179 tow ($125 hook-up + 9 loaded miles at $6), sent now. A card is saved on the secure page and charged $179 when Kyle texts DONE at the shop. The $89 dry-run fee is kept only for a late cancel or a no-show, if Sam confirms it.

services.name: Roadside tow for a motor club
services.story: A motor club or insurer's roadside plan pays the company directly: nothing is taken from Alex, and Sam bills the plan his own way.

questions_before_times: Is anyone hurt? Is the car in a traffic lane? Any smoke? (Any yes: 911 first, no booking)
Where are you: the road, the direction, an exit or mile marker? (The exact spot comes from the phone, on the secure page.)
Whose car is it: yours, or one you drive with the owner's OK? (A rental: the rental company's roadside line first.)
The car: year, make, model and color. Is it all-wheel drive?
What happened: won't start, a flat, out of fuel, locked out, or a crash?
Where should it go: a shop, home, or the yard?
How many people need a ride: none, 1 or 2?
Does a motor club or insurer's roadside plan pay? (Just its name here.)
safety_stop: a crash, or a car stopped in a traffic lane
smoke, fire or a fuel smell
a child or a pet left inside the car
license: Where the state's rules require it: a towing permit or license for the company (some states also want one per truck), and a tow operator license for each driver. Trucks that cross state lines may need a federal carrier (USDOT) number. Where none is required: identity checked, and 'license: what the business says'.
